races.name: Celebrate National Racehorse Week 2026 Mares' Maiden Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Diamond Grace
runners_data.note: Sole natural front-runner, Jonjo O'Neill Jr. will exploit the uncontested lead immediately; two placed efforts on good ground sim-going (2/3) and 41 days fresh suggest she arrives fit and ready to exploit a weak pace dynamic.

runners_data.name: Dreaming Of The Dr
runners_data.note: Unknown style mapped here with no prominent or lead tendencies; Luke Scott (3) on a trainer with a poor 14-day record (0/7), and three recent finishes of 4th-7th on good-to-soft suggest a horse yet to find her method over hurdles at this level.

runners_data.name: La Bamba Chica
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 130 days off for Jim & Suzi Best, with only one hurdle start on record (5th on good); Richie McLernon will seek to hold a close tracking position, and the good-to-firm conditions match her one run of sim-going experience.

runners_data.name: Letmeseethecolts
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator who has placed three times from six runs on similar ground, including a win, giving her the best sim-going strike rate in the field; Nathan Moscrop will likely settle last or second-last, meaning she needs the gallop to be stronger than Diamond Grace is likely to offer.

runners_data.name: Pretty Spontaneous
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and carrying a going-unknown flag plus a tongue-tie, her form string of PF5-PP is deeply uninspiring and Chad Bament (5) is a significant claim; style is genuinely uncertain, making her the biggest wildcard in the race.

runners_data.name: Guts And Glory
runners_data.note: Stan Sheppard partners this four-year-old who has placed twice on soft from a prominent position, but the step up to good-to-firm on a more galloping track is an untested variable; the tongue-tie remains and 136 days off the track adds a fitness question.

runners_data.name: Princess Of Ballea
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile who has yet to finish better than third from six hurdle starts, repeatedly posting mid-to-rear finishes on good ground (5/6 sim-going, 0W2P); Harry Reed will need the pace to be genuinely taxing for a late run to land.

runners_data.name: Steal A Glance
runners_data.note: Sam Twiston-Davies on an off-pace type whose form reads 73-955 — no win, one third, and consistent mid-division finishes on good ground; the tongue-tie is retained and the step to 2m2½f on good-to-firm may not unlock the improvement needed to beat a well-placed front-runner.

races.paceDynamic: Diamond Grace is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no other horse in the field showing a natural desire to lead, she will set off in front unchallenged and dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground at Stratford. La Bamba Chica and Guts And Glory will push up to track her in prominent positions, while Steal A Glance may also press forward from her off-pace profile, but none carries the profile or the jockey intent to seriously contest the lead. The result is a single-file, uncontested lead scenario where Diamond Grace can conserve energy through the early stages, control the tempo through the final bend, and present a moving target that hold-up horses will struggle to reel in unless the pace collapses entirely. This race shape strongly favours the front-runner and close trackers — horses who can sit just off the pace in positions two or three, travel comfortably, and produce a measured jump at the last; genuine hold-up types are at a structural disadvantage given the likely moderate early fractions that will not string the field out early enough for a late burst to count.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls All
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Grace settles into her rhythm unchallenged and the pace proves steady-to-moderate throughout.
scenarios.body: Diamond Grace bowls along in front, the field strings out behind her without ever applying meaningful pressure, and she arrives at the last with enough in reserve to repel the chasers; her good-to-firm form (2/3 sim-going) and OR of 95 in a field of OR-120 mares who have repeatedly failed to win underlines her tactical edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Grace sets a slightly stronger gallop than usual and a prominent-position horse finishes with more resolution over the final two flights.
scenarios.body: La Bamba Chica or Guts And Glory sit in second or third throughout, travel without fuss on good-to-firm, and collar a tiring Diamond Grace approaching the last; both have previously finished second from off-pace prominent roles and the good ground suits their jumping.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely strong and the front-runners tie each other up, creating a punishing pace that leaves the lead group vulnerable.
scenarios.body: Letmeseethecolts or Princess Of Ballea, the only genuine hold-up runners in the field, would be the logical beneficiaries of a truly searching gallop, producing their finishing effort over the final flight; however, neither has converted prominent finishing positions into wins at this level, and the structural disadvantage of a moderate-to-steady expected pace makes this a low-probability path.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unexpected Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Grace makes a critical jumping error early or is pulled up, fundamentally reshaping the race with no natural front-runner left in the field.
scenarios.body: La Bamba Chica or Steal A Glance would be forced to the front reluctantly, creating a chaotic, bunched finish where the most adaptable jumper prevails; Guts And Glory's hurdle form (two seconds from 16f on soft) shows she copes when circumstances change, making her a possible beneficiary of race-shape chaos.

watchPoints.text: Diamond Grace is the only confirmed front-runner — if she jumps cleanly at the first two hurdles and settles into her rhythm, the race is effectively hers to lose from the front.
La Bamba Chica returns from 130 days off and, if Jim & Suzi Best have her fit enough, Richie McLernon tracking Diamond Grace in second could be the most dangerous position in the race late on.
Pretty Spontaneous's going flag and lightly raced status make her a genuine unknown quantity — watch the market closely for any late move that suggests Anthony Honeyball has her ready.
Letmeseethecolts has the best sim-going win/place record in the field (1W3P from 6) but is entirely dependent on a searching gallop that Diamond Grace is not expected to provide.
Guts And Glory has not run for 136 days and has no form on ground quicker than soft — monitor paddock behaviour and early jumping for signs the four-year-old is handling the conditions.

races.name: Stratford Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Bells Of Ufford
runners_data.note: Has placed twice at this 20f trip on good ground and profiles as one of the more credible hold-up closers here; Tim Vaughan's runners have been quiet (0/1 in 14 days) but the horse's similar-going record (0W2P from 13 runs) suggests competitiveness without a genuine win threat, and 46 days off is not a concern at this level.
runners_data.comment: Bells Of Ufford is winless in his last five starts but that second two runs back is the most telling piece of form in the race, and our rating of 93 just edges the field; 46 days off should have him fresh and ready to go under 166 lb.

runners_data.name: Brionywells
runners_data.note: Two wins from 11 runs on good ground make this Nick Slatter's most interesting booking — the horse stays well and has form at 23f — though 74 days between runs is notable and McPherson/Killahena's poor 14-day record (0/6) adds a marginal fitness flag; a true hold-up type who needs things to set up late.
runners_data.comment: Brionywells landed back-to-back wins two and three starts back and has run over today's trip, making her a live threat off a mark of 90, though the 74-day absence is the one factor to weigh against her.

runners_data.name: Captain Connor
runners_data.note: Consistently finishing 7th-8th at shorter trips and without a win or place on similar going (0W0P from 6 sim-going runs), this horse's entire CV points to a hold-up operator out of its depth here; Clare Ellam sends out just one runner and the STYLE_FIT tag reinforces that mapping this horse to midfield on the diagram overstates its likely engagement.
runners_data.comment: Rated higher than his official mark suggests, Captain Connor arrives here with conditions that could bring out the best in him, though his recent string of disappointing efforts — including a pull-up in his last five starts — remains the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: French Diablo
runners_data.note: The only horse in the field who genuinely wants to lead, and his best effort — a win at 22f on good — fits this assignment well; David Bass is a capable front-riding partner for Max Comley, and the STYLE_FIT tag applies because the mapping positions him as prominent when his natural role is to dominate; on 44 days' rest and with 1W2P from 5 similar-going runs, he is the shape-setter.
runners_data.comment: French Diablo won last time out but his record in recent starts also includes a pull-up, and our rating ranks him sixth of eight here; he has run over today's trip and going before, yet 154 lb makes the task no easier.

runners_data.name: Delgany Second Now
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton is the headline here — a top-level jockey on a Dan Skelton yard in flying form (6/23 in 14 days) — but the horse has finished 5th-7th in all four hurdle runs and genuinely prefers to come from off the pace; the redistribution to midfield on the map reflects that the rear is congested, and a STYLE_FIT discount is warranted given its modest form at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Delgany Second Now arrives here after 34 days off carrying 153 lb, and a mark of 81 suggests the handicapper holds him in check, though his trainer's current 26% strike rate over the last fortnight offers a timely positive.

runners_data.name: Kotgar
runners_data.note: Three runs at 18f+ showing a 3rd and a 5th suggest Kotgar stays the trip but lacks the class to capitalise; Mrs C Williams sends it with a quiet 14-day record (0/2) and Conor Ring will be looking to produce from hold-up but the horse's sim-going record (0W2P from 11 runs) signals a place-only profile at best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Kotgar nonetheless shaped with promise when third last time out and has experience of today's going in his favour, making him a genuine threat off 149 lb; the risk is whether he can finally convert that placed effort into something more decisive.

runners_data.name: Mc'flo
runners_data.note: A P (pulled up) on the most recent run flags a stamina or jumping concern, and the overall form string — 8964P — is unrelentingly poor across good-ground trips from 20f to 23f; Anthony Carson's yard is cold (0/1 in 14 days) and this horse's redistribution to midfield on the map disguises a true hold-up style that has delivered nothing competitive.
runners_data.comment: Mc'flo has been winless in her last five starts, pulling up most recently, and ranked seventh of eight on our figures she faces a stiff task here; she does arrive fit enough at 30 days since her last run and has experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Pink Walls
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner at OR=60 and operating at a significant class deficit, Pink Walls has finished 4th on good ground at 22f but has a string of poor efforts otherwise; Kevin Brogan takes over the ride and the horse's redistribution from the back of the field is purely a mapping artefact — it is a genuine hold-up type with no realistic winning scenario on current evidence.
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and unexposed, Pink Walls has shown little in recent starts — a pair of pull-ups and an eighth among her last five — but with 44 days between runs and open to improvement, she merits watching if she settles and completes the course.

races.paceDynamic: French Diablo is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 2m6f novice hurdle on good-to-firm ground at Stratford, and with no genuine rival willing or able to press him from the outset, David Bass can dictate a controlled, galloping tempo that suits a horse who won over course-and-distance-equivalent ground on his best effort. The remainder of the field — Bells Of Ufford, Brionywells, Captain Connor, Delgany Second Now, Kotgar, Mc'flo and Pink Walls — are all natural hold-up or wait-and-see types, meaning French Diablo will face zero early pressure and can dictate every yard of the race. This field holds far more genuine hold-up horses than the map can position at the rear; Captain Connor, Delgany Second Now, Kotgar and Mc'flo are all true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map, with Harry Skelton on Delgany Second Now and Brendan Powell on Captain Connor the most likely to push forward relative to their rivals, though neither will genuinely challenge French Diablo for the lead. An uncontested, class-conscious front-runner over a stamina-testing trip on quick ground is the dominant shape here, and horses with the class and jumping ability to track French Diablo at a comfortable distance — or to grind him down late from a prominent position — are the profile to favour.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: French Diablo Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If French Diablo bowls along in front unchallenged and sets a sensible gallop that dries up stamina reserves in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: French Diablo controls the tempo under David Bass, jumping efficiently around Stratford's tight turns, and any horse hoping to close must do so without the benefit of cover or a true target to aim at. Horses with proven class at this trip and the ability to track at a distance — Brionywells and Bells Of Ufford — are best placed to benefit if French Diablo ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Late
scenarios.trigger: If French Diablo's early dominance sets a fast enough clip that his stamina gives way in the final half-mile, inviting a grinding late challenge.
scenarios.body: On good-to-firm ground over 2m6f, even a well-judged front-running display can leave a horse vulnerable to strong-travelling hold-up types who have been buried in the pack conserving energy. Brionywells, who has won twice at this sort of trip and going, and Bells Of Ufford, who has shown positional aptitude, are the likeliest beneficiaries of a late collapse.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistibuted midfield horses — most likely Delgany Second Now under Harry Skelton — pushes forward enough to track French Diablo and outstays him from second.
scenarios.body: Skelton is a trainer-jockey combination known for forcing position on hold-up types when the opportunity presents itself, and Delgany Second Now's moderate flat form masks a horse that may stay this far better than rivals. However, the horse's consistent finishing positions in the 5-7 range and a STYLE_FIT discount temper expectation significantly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos At The Jumps
scenarios.trigger: If multiple jumping errors or falls disrupt the shape of the race and compress the field, negating French Diablo's positional advantage.
scenarios.body: Novice hurdle fields over this trip on fast ground are vulnerable to erratic jumping, and a disrupted race could see the field bunch and the front-runner lose his rhythm and advantage. Pink Walls and Mc'flo, operating well below French Diablo's class level, are unlikely to profit from chaos but are the longest-priced beneficiaries if the race falls apart entirely.

watchPoints.text: French Diablo is the sole pace-setter and if David Bass gets his jumping right in the early stages and reaches the home straight with his energy intact, he could prove extremely difficult to reel in over this stamina-testing 2m6f.
Brionywells has 74 days between runs and the trainer's 0/6 form over the past 14 days raises a fitness question — watch the market for any drift that signals connections are uncertain heading in.

Delgany Second Now under Harry Skelton is the most dangerous redistributed hold-up type in the race; watch at the start and first few flights to see whether Skelton forces position forward, which would materially change the shape of the race.

With seven of eight runners being genuine hold-up types, the race could become densely packed in the middle stages — watch for jumping incidents at the tighter Stratford turns that could compress or disrupt the field and bring a long-shot into contention.

Good-to-firm ground confirmed throughout the card at Stratford; any horse whose trainer has flagged going concerns or who has a poor record on faster surfaces should be monitored closely in the going-to-post inspections, particularly those with softer-ground form strings.

races.name: George & Dragon Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Duke Of Luckley
runners_data.note: Martin Keighley's nine-year-old has strong credentials on this going (14/15 similar-going record, 5 wins) and his prominent style maps perfectly to the predicted race shape — son Freddie Keighley rides and the pair know each other well; 32 days since last run is a non-issue given the yard's 1/3 recent form, and the blinkers underline he is kept sharp.
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner three starts back, with a third two starts back boosting his claims, Duke Of Luckley lines up after 32 days off carrying 168 lb and has run over today's trip; he rates the one to beat on these terms.

runners_data.name: Seeyouinmydreams
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: T Ellis sends out this eight-year-old with an uncontested lead in prospect and his good-ground record (11/15, 4 wins) backs up his chance of lasting home; the tongue-tie is retained, the trip is his bread and butter at 16-19f on similar ground, and Jack Andrews is a confident booking for an unpressed leader.
runners_data.comment: Seeyouinmydreams shaped well for a third three starts back before landing a win four starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going underpin a strong each-way case; the 165 lb burden is the one factor that could anchor her.

runners_data.name: Beorma
runners_data.note: Six wins from six starts is a remarkable sequence and Harry Skelton's handling of this seven-year-old for Dan Skelton's red-hot yard is the principal threat to the front pair; the 67-day layoff is the only mild flag, but the tongue-tie is retained and good ground (10/15, 7 wins) suits — the issue is whether a dawdle off the pace on a tight track leaves him with too much to do.
runners_data.comment: Six wins in her last six starts make Beorma a formidable proposition, and a trainer firing at 26% bolsters her claims considerably, with experience over today's trip another tick in her favour; the main concern is a 67-day absence carrying a hefty 160 lb.

runners_data.name: In This World
runners_data.note: B R Summers has no runners in the last 14 days to gauge form, and the 87-day break combined with a recent run sequence of 4P5-5F and a fall makes this runner the clear outsider on any pace-shape reading; James Best will try to make the best of a hold-up position, but the class gap and raw form make significant involvement unlikely regardless of how the race unfolds.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and carrying 156 lb, In This World has run over today's trip and a rating of 119 suggests he holds strong claims as a leading danger; the fall last time out is the one obvious concern.

races.paceDynamic: Seeyouinmydreams is the sole confirmed front-runner in this four-runner field and will stride into the lead unchallenged from the outset, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop over 2m1f on Good to Firm ground at Stratford. Duke Of Luckley will track prominently just behind, whilst Beorma and In This World are both hold-up types who will settle in the rear and rely on picking up late ground. With no rival to press Seeyouinmydreams, the pace is unlikely to be testing, creating a steady-run contest where the front-runner dictates every gear change and the closers face a longer task to close the gap in the straight. This race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-front profile — specifically a horse travelling within striking distance of a lone, uncontested leader — because a truly steady gallop on quick ground at a sharp track like Stratford tends to reward those who can pounce at the second-last rather than those grinding from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Front Pair Win
scenarios.trigger: If Seeyouinmydreams dictates an unchallenged, measured gallop and the closers cannot bridge the gap from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Seeyouinmydreams sets fractions that suit his stamina profile perfectly on quick ground, and Duke Of Luckley, travelling prominently throughout, is ideally placed to pounce if the leader weakens late; the hold-up pair are simply too far back on a sharp 2m1f circuit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Tiring Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Seeyouinmydreams sets a slightly faster-than-expected pace and ties himself up before the last, allowing the hold-up pair to close.
scenarios.body: Beorma's unbeaten six-run form sequence and Harry Skelton's tactical acumen make him the most dangerous of the closers if the pace lifts sufficiently to bring him into play; Skelton can engineer gaps on a turning track and Beorma's 16f good-ground wins show raw ability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Beorma Makes Smooth Move
scenarios.trigger: If Beorma travels supremely well off the steady pace and Skelton produces him early enough to dominate before the final fence.
scenarios.body: Dan Skelton's yard is firing at 6/23 over 14 days and Beorma's six consecutive wins suggest a horse at the peak of his powers who could defy a hold-up tag if produced with a well-timed sweeping run; the concern is whether a genuinely slow pace gives him enough to reel in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: In This World Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace completely collapses and In This World, the lowest-rated runner, produces a surprise finish from the back.
scenarios.body: In This World's recent form reads 4P5-5F and a 87-day absence makes this scenario deeply unlikely, requiring everything to go wrong for the principals; even in a chaotic race his class ceiling looks well below the others.

watchPoints.text: Watch Seeyouinmydreams's jumping — if he makes a costly error at any of the early fences on the run away from the stands, Duke Of Luckley could inherit a free lead and control the race himself.

Monitor Beorma's position leaving the back straight: if Harry Skelton has not moved into third by the time they turn for home, the hold-up horse will almost certainly run out of Stratford's short run-in to pounce.

In This World's 87-day absence combined with a fall in his last completed run is a significant safety flag — watch for any sign of jumping hesitancy at the early fences that could cause interference for the small field.

With only four runners, any jumping error by Seeyouinmydreams in the final half-mile transforms this from a controlled leader's race into a blanket finish, so his fence-jumping quality at the end of the race is the single most important visual cue.

races.name: Allsopps Love Stratford Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: T Or Coffey
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer whose best Stratford runs have come at this exact trip and on good ground, making the going no concern; Jennie Candlish's five-year-old needs the pace to lift for Lewis Stones to deliver his finishing effort from the rear, which is far from guaranteed with Getmyfriend going steady up front.
runners_data.comment: T Or Coffey won two starts back and was third three starts back, showing he can compete at this level, but a sixth last time out after 34 days off raises a fitness query, and 168 lb is a significant burden for a horse ranked fifth of eight here.

runners_data.name: Borna Gem
runners_data.note: Nigel and Willy Twiston-Davies's seven-year-old returns from 128 days off — the most notable freshness flag in this field — but has winning form on good ground over this distance and Miss Jackson-Fennell's 7lb claim is a significant weight relief for a horse who can race prominently and challenge on the bridle.
runners_data.comment: Borna Gem won two starts back but has pulled up and been brought down in between, leaving her profile hard to read, and 128 days off the track adds further uncertainty; she has run over today's trip and a rating of 99 offers some hope, though ninth last time out tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Zucayan
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien's nine-year-old is a hold-up horse who showed a fall on his last outing and wears a tongue-tie; his similar-going record of one win from fifteen starts suggests he finds this surface merely adequate, and Nick Slatter picks him up having also been off only 33 days, needing a genuine end-to-end gallop that this race will not produce.
runners_data.comment: Zucayan shaped with plenty of promise when second two starts back and again three starts back, and he returns here fresh after 33 days off having run over today's trip before; yet to score in recent starts, but his profile over this distance and conditions makes him our pick.

runners_data.name: Getmyfriend
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner, trained in sharp form by Dan Skelton (6 wins from 23 in the last 14 days) and ridden by Harry Skelton, who has four wins from five on good ground with this horse; at OR 101 he is top of the weights but controls every tactical variable in this race.
runners_data.comment: Getmyfriend won last time out and has previous experience over today's trip and going, arriving from a yard firing at 26% over the past fortnight; the risk is that 164 lb is a hefty weight to carry.

runners_data.name: Juggernaut
runners_data.note: Anthony Honeyball's seven-year-old has finished second or third in six of his last nine starts and is a consistent but non-threatening prominent type who trades heavily on his reliability rather than ability to quicken; James Robottom's 10lb claim offsets the weight, but course form over longer trips at this venue does not fully translate here.

runners_data.name: Dream Jet
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's eight-year-old is in truth a hold-up horse whose instinct is to be delivered late, but with the rear of the field congested by multiple hold-up types he sits in midfield on the map — a position that blunts his natural style; his style-fit discount is real, and a STYLE_FIT score of 0.94 tempers enthusiasm despite reasonable recent form figures.
runners_data.comment: Dream Jet arrives on the back of a fourth last time out, with a third three starts back hinting at the ability to mix it at this level, and our rating of 103 slots him comfortably into contention despite carrying 160 lb; the risk is that he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Mi Sueno
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's seven-year-old ran only three days ago — the freshness concern here runs in reverse, with potential fatigue a factor — but two recent wins on good ground over this sort of trip show genuine ability, and racing prominently from a light weight of 142lbs gives Harry Reed every chance to slot in just off the leader.
runners_data.comment: Mi Sueno returns just three days after his last outing, which raises a stamina-for-recovery question, and ranked eighth of eight on our figures he faces a stiff ask; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a win two starts back offers a crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Miss Fedora
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up performer who at OR 75 is the bottom weight alongside Mi Sueno; her true instinct is to be produced late, but she is effectively displaced to midfield because the back of the field is crowded — Benjamin Macey's 5lb claim helps marginally, and her good-ground figures (STYLE_FIT 0.91) suggest any chance is further diluted by racing out of her preferred role.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Miss Fedora offers little encouragement — a record featuring two pulled-ups and a refusal is deeply concerning. Her experience over today's trip and going is a minor positive, but she faces a stiff ask.

races.paceDynamic: Getmyfriend is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, ridden by Harry Skelton, will stride directly into the lead from the gates on good-to-firm ground at Stratford, a track that rewards prominent, jumping horses who can control tempo. With no genuine challenger disputing the early lead, Getmyfriend sets a sustainable, metronomic gallop that is unlikely to be pressured into anything suicidal, making this a classic single-pace, controlled-lead scenario. Borna Gem, Juggernaut, and Mi Sueno will track up in the prominent pack, while T Or Coffey and Zucayan are genuine hold-up types who will need the pace to quicken materially in the closing stages to deliver their finishing kicks. This field holds more hold-up horses than can realistically secure a position at the rear — Dream Jet and Miss Fedora, both true hold-up types, have been pushed into midfield slots on the map because the rear berths are overcrowded, meaning their natural late-run game is compromised. This race shape overwhelmingly favours a prominent runner who can travel fluently close to the leader and time a challenge from the second-last hurdle onward.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Getmyfriend Controls And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Getmyfriend jumps cleanly, dictates an uncontested moderate pace, and quickens from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Harry Skelton's mount has won twice on good ground over similar trips and faces zero pace pressure, allowing him to conserve energy and produce a telling jump at the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Getmyfriend's lead is close enough that a prominent traveller picks him off after the last hurdle.
scenarios.body: Borna Gem or Mi Sueno, sitting a length or two off the pace throughout, produces a fluent jump at the final hurdle and edges ahead on the run-in on the fast ground that suits both.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Fast
scenarios.trigger: If Getmyfriend sets a genuinely strong enough gallop that hold-up horses finish with real momentum.
scenarios.body: T Or Coffey, whose course-and-distance form is solid and who won over similar Stratford trips, or Zucayan, are the most credible beneficiaries if pace genuinely rises, though the single-pacer makes this less likely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Carnage And Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or jumping errors scramble the race entirely, leaving a non-obvious winner.
scenarios.body: Dream Jet or Miss Fedora — both displaced from their natural hold-up positions and carrying style-fit discounts — could stumble into contention if the field is decimated, though neither is ideally positioned for this race shape.

watchPoints.text: Getmyfriend jumping — Harry Skelton's mount must clear every hurdle cleanly at the head of affairs; a single jumping error at a critical point hands the initiative to Borna Gem or Mi Sueno who are tracking right behind.
Mi Sueno ran just three days ago; watch for any sign of blowiness or a flat effort from the two-mile marker, which would remove one of the most credible prominent threats from the equation.
Borna Gem returns from 128 days absent — if she shows any ring rustiness in the early stages and drops further back than her natural prominent style demands, her chance narrows sharply.

Dream Jet and Miss Fedora are both racing out of their ideal hold-up positions; if the pace does not lift materially in the final circuit, neither will generate the momentum needed to reach the front pair, and their odds should be treated with caution accordingly.

The going report confirms Good To Firm across all distances at Stratford today — faster than the declared Good — which emphasises fluent jumping and prominent positioning even more strongly than the map already suggests.

races.name: Thank You To Our Hardworking Groundstaff Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Bobbarelli
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a solid placed record on similar going (6/7 sim-going runs in the frame); wears hood and headgear combination, aged 9 but consistent, and his 75-day break looks unlikely to blunt his natural jumping enthusiasm from the front.
runners_data.comment: Consistent place-getter Bobbarelli has been second or third in three of his last four starts, and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims as the top-rated runner here; the 75-day break and a disappointing ninth last time out are the only notes of caution under a big 168 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Youdecide
runners_data.note: 151 days off the track is the dominant concern here — form reads F444P on last five and he has a pull in the weights, but absence from competition at this level on good ground makes him a significant unknown; hold-up style may suit if the pace truly burns.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 151 days off, Youdecide nonetheless carries a rating of 102 to suggest he holds strong claims at this level, and he has run over today's trip before; the pull-up last time out is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Jack Doyen
runners_data.note: Well-credentialled prominent racer with two recent wins at similar distances on comparable going; wears blinkers, runs for Ben Case who has a 1/4 T14 strike rate, and his consistency across 2m4f-2m6f trips makes him the most dangerous tracking horse in the field.
runners_data.comment: Jack Doyen arrives on the back of a first last time out, and a winner three times in his last five starts overall, with strong recent form that marks him out as a genuine danger; the chief concern is a 98-day absence on his return.

runners_data.name: Pescatorius
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer whose last five runs show strong staying-ground form at distances from 2m4f to 2m6f; wears a tongue-tie, trainer has no runners in the T14 window, and a 83-day break will need to be taken on trust, but the good-to-firm going is within range.
runners_data.comment: Pescatorius has shown he can compete at this level with thirds latest and three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset off a mark of 88 — the main concern is 83 days off the track without a win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Crackerjack Queen
runners_data.note: Returned just 34 days ago and has a fair record on good ground, winning at 2m4f last season; her natural instinct is to race from the rear but in this pace-heavy field she is unlikely to find that position naturally, which tempers expectations despite the tongue and blinkers headgear combination.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but a placed effort three runs back offers some encouragement, and she has run over today's trip before; at 149 lb, the weight is a notable ask as she bids to break through.

runners_data.name: Kings Order
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with limited jumping experience compared to rivals and a patchy record including an 11th on soft; a genuine hold-up horse by inclination who won't easily slot into his preferred berth given the field's pace profile, and the tongue-tie hasn't yet unlocked a win.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of eight on our figures, Kings Order arrives after a 57-day break carrying 145 lb, making him hard to fancy despite a third last time out and experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Watchoutitscookie
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with five recent placed finishes on good ground at distances around 2m3f-2m4f — slightly shorter than today; David Noonan is capable at this level and the 37-day freshness is a mild plus, though the 2m5f trip is a step beyond his most recent form.
runners_data.comment: Watchoutitscookie has run over today's trip and going, and a third last time out suggests he retains some ability, though he remains winless in his last five starts and carries 142 lb, which tests his resolution here.

runners_data.name: Fox Wallace
runners_data.note: Confirmed lead-seeker whose trainer has no T14 runners and 151 sim-going runs in the database showing 1 win — moderate overall; wears a tongue-tie and has been placed on similar going, but OR of 69 means he is contributing pace rather than posing a serious winning threat.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, including two pulls up, Fox Wallace faces a stiff ask ranked seventh of eight on our figures, though she has run over today's going before and 38 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Bobbarelli and Fox Wallace are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off, with neither likely to concede ground willingly on this good-to-firm Stratford surface over 2m5f. The resulting pace should be honest rather than frantic — two leaders trading blows across the opening mile will set a genuine gallop that tests stamina into the final circuit. Jack Doyen and Watchoutitscookie sit just off that pace in prominent positions, meaning the race has a clear and continuous engine from start to finish, rewarding those who travel well through it rather than those who switch off at the rear. The tactical verdict is clear: this shape strongly favours hold-up horses who possess genuine relentless galloping ability and can pick off tiring front-runners in the closing stages — horses with strong staying profiles and good form on similar going. This field carries more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear; Crackerjack Queen and Kings Order are genuine hold-up horses by inclination but have been redistributed to midfield on the map — Bobbarelli and Fox Wallace are the ones who will actually control the early tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Stretch Field
scenarios.trigger: If Bobbarelli and Fox Wallace maintain a genuine contested lead and grind rivals into submission on the good-to-firm ground.
scenarios.body: The two leaders share the work at a relentless gallop that saps the finishing kicks of hold-up horses who can't close from too far back; whoever of the two leads pairs is stronger in the last half-mile wins or finishes placed. Bobbarelli's course-compatible form and consistent placed record on similar going makes him the natural beneficiary if the gallop is truly wearing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the contested front-running pace burns out the leaders in the final mile and a prominent tracker conserves enough energy to overhaul them.
scenarios.body: Jack Doyen, with three wins at similar distances and excellent form on good ground, is ideally placed to stalk the lead pair and strike when they crack; Watchoutitscookie has the fitness and track experience over comparable trips to be a secondary beneficiary here. This is the shape that most rewards a horse who races three or four lengths off the pace without cover, travelling with purpose throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-running battle is unusually fierce and genuine hold-up horses get a strong enough gallop to close from off the pace in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Pescatorius has placed twice on good ground at distances around 2m4f-2m6f and possesses the staying profile to benefit from a true-run race; Youdecide, despite 151 days off, is the unknown quantity whose fresh-horse energy could see a late dash. Note that Crackerjack Queen and Kings Order — the redistibuted hold-up types — are not truly racing from their natural position in this map and their ability to execute a wide closing run is consequently compromised.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Chaos Late Errors
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or falls thin the field in the closing stages and an unlikely survivor collects.
scenarios.body: Fencing mistakes on good-to-firm can unseat front-runners mid-race at Stratford's stiff fences, opening the door for lower-rated survivors; Kings Order and Crackerjack Queen, though racing out of their true hold-up roles at the rear, could both collect a minor prize if the field is decimated ahead of them. This is a low-probability chaos scenario rather than a structured race shape.

watchPoints.text: Bobbarelli and Fox Wallace will lock horns early — watch which one capitulates first, as the loser of that duel is likely to weaken dramatically in the final mile and create interference risks at the fences.
Jack Doyen's blinkers suggest he can be keen early — if he gets sucked into the front-running battle rather than sitting prominent, his chance of a late run is significantly compromised.

Youdecide has not run for 151 days and his last five runs include two falls/pulled-up finishes — monitor his jumping closely in the early stages as a jumping blunder from a cold horse could cause serious interference from the rear.

Good-to-firm ground at Stratford places a premium on accurate fencing — Fox Wallace has a recent history of jumping errors and a mistake at a critical fence on the final circuit would open the race up to the tracking pair of Jack Doyen and Watchoutitscookie.

Crackerjack Queen and Kings Order are both lower-class hold-up horses whose redistribution to midfield means they face a race where their chance depends on an untypically aggressive jumping display — watch whether they actually track up or drift back as the race settles.

races.name: Hollow Bottom National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (Conditional & Amateur Jockeys) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Company Charge
runners_data.comment: Company Charge has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 97 makes him a genuine threat from a field of nine, yet he arrives on the back of a fifth last time out and is winless in recent starts, with 43 days off the sharpest potential concern.

runners_data.name: Goliath Power
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Goliath Power arrives as a complete unknown carrying 156 lb, and with no public form to dissect he is open to any level of improvement his first start brings.

runners_data.name: Bombus Pascuorum
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Bombus Pascuorum arrives as a complete unknown and carrying 153 lb, yet to score but open to any amount of improvement as connections get their first look at him in a race environment.

runners_data.name: On The Fly
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, On The Fly steps back up after 41 days off carrying 153 lb, yet to score in recent starts but lightly raced enough that there could be considerably more to come.

runners_data.name: Stand Proud
runners_data.comment: Stand Proud has experience over today's trip and returns after 41 days off carrying 153 lb, with our rating of 90 making him a credible threat in a field of nine; the concern is that he heads here winless on the back of an eighth last time out.

runners_data.name: Talladale
runners_data.comment: Talladale arrives as the top-rated runner in this field of nine, and having run over today's trip before, he lines up with relevant experience to draw on; yet to land a win in recent starts, the 41-day break and 153 lb burden are the questions his supporters must answer.

runners_data.name: Guerdale
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last two starts, with an eighth and a sixth, Guerdale faces a stiff ask ranked fifth of nine on our figures, and 51 days off the track adds further doubt; experience over today's trip is at least something to cling to.

runners_data.name: Pearl Cove
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement after just two starts, Pearl Cove returns from 41 days off yet to win and will be sharper for that experience, with her light campaign suggesting there is plenty more to come.

runners_data.name: Roccana Rose
runners_data.comment: Roccana Rose catches the eye on rating, ranking second of nine here, and has run over today's trip before, giving her an experience edge; the main concern is a lengthy 83-day absence leaving fitness an open question.
